comment: R4 cost sheet: dated unit prices by category and named scenarios. Prices are AWS on-demand list prices for us-east-1 as known to the release lane on the as_of date, NOT fetched from the Pricing API (no AWS call in R4). Confirm each in the AWS Pricing Calculator before an approval. tools/lifecycle.py reads this file; tools/plan_review.py cost keeps reading cost_assumptions.json.

disk.unit: GiB-month, gp3 (3000 IOPS / 125 MB/s baseline included)

ipv4.unit: public IPv4 address-hour, in use or idle

logs.unit: CloudWatch Logs GiB ingested, GiB-month stored; alarm-month

staging-pass.note: one synthetic staging pass, power-off after 4 h, destroyed the same day

staging-not-destroyed-7d.note: the power-off ends compute at 4 h; terminate deletes the root disk; the data volume and the bucket stay 7 days until someone runs terraform destroy

production-month.note: always on; 35 daily backups of about 100 MB in S3; two EC2 alarms; no CloudWatch Logs (journald on the host)

production-peak-month.note: t3.medium (for example the speech sidecar), 50 GiB data, hourly backups kept 7 days, a 20 GiB weekly snapshot, 1 GiB/month of CloudWatch Logs

assumptions: Data transfer: the SSM port forward and S3 through the gateway endpoint stay inside the free tier at one learner's volume; not costed.
SSM Parameter Store (standard) and Session Manager: free.
IPv4 is billed per hour while associated; the auto-assigned public address is released on stop or terminate, so it stops billing with the instance.
No Elastic IP, NAT gateway, load balancer, CloudFront or Route 53 resource exists in this root (plan_check STOPs on them).
Taxes, support plans and the provider usage (OpenAI) are outside this sheet.
